lexical.anchor: **`GK-16` means Sañjaya in one document and Guṇa in the other. `GK-09` means Sañjaya in one and Buddhi in the other.** ... **This is the same defect class as the `H-K04`/`H-K06` collision — now at the GK level and *across two documents*, which is worse: a cross-document citation of `GK-16` is unresolvable.**

rationale_evidence.anchor: **`GK-16`** | **Guṇa** | **Sañjaya** | ⚠️ **worst.** Sañjaya is the observation-layer recovery; Guṇa is an unopened measurement item. **A citation of `GK-16` could mean the strongest finding or an unexamined one**
rationale_evidence.statement: Identifies GK-16 as the single worst collision: it means Guna (an unopened, unexamined measurement item) in v0.1 but Sanjaya (the major observation-layer recovery finding) in r286 — a bare citation of GK-16 could refer to either the strongest finding in the whole research programme or an item nobody has yet examined.
